jobs.title: Drift Wood #5 · the review
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 17, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; CHLOE — aged 17, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders, oversized dark cardigan, a Discman on her belt with headphones around her neck, a folded-back paperback, reads while talking. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Chloe reviews the fall play. Wood reviews the review. Panel 1: a teenage girl typing at a beige 1990s computer in a school newsroom while a boy in an overcoat reads a printout over her shoulder (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). Wood says "You gave the fall play two stars.". Panel 2: close-up of a teenage girl typing, unbothered, eyeliner smudged (in this panel: CHLOE). Chloe says "I gave it two stars because it was two stars. Danny Voss forgot his lines and then did them in the wrong act.". Panel 3: a teenage boy pacing in a newsroom with one arm out mid-speech, overcoat swinging (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "Criticism should elevate. Bazin didn't give stars. He gave a way of seeing.". Panel 4: a teenage girl holding up a printed review with a red-pen note crossed out at the bottom, a boy in an overcoat caught mid-protest (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). Chloe says "You added a note. Then you agreed with me.". Wood says "Bazin would have—". Chloe says "Two.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
